The weight of the box is given by \( mg \), where \( m \) is the mass of the box and \( g \) is the acceleration due to gravity. The component of the weight perpendicular to the plane is \( mg \cos(\theta) \), and the component parallel to the plane is \( mg \sin(\theta) \).

\[ N = mg \cos(\theta) \]

Therefore, the normal force decreases nonlinearly as the angle of the inclined plane increases.

The key idea here is that when you have two different wavelengths (a doublet), the path difference between the two beams will cause interference patterns that change as you move one of the mirrors. This should relate to the difference in wavelengths, λ�� and λ₂.

In a Michelson interferometer, the fringe pattern shifts by one fringe when the mirror is moved by a distance equal to half the wavelength (λ/2). But here, we have two wavelengths, so this should relate to the difference in wavelengths.

When the mirror is moved by a distance Δx, the optical path difference changes by 2Δx (since the light travels back and forth in the interferometer arm). For the interference pattern to repeat (i.e., the contrast variations to be periodic), the path difference change should be an integer multiple of the smallest wavelength difference. Wait, more precisely, the condition for the fringe contrast to vary periodically as the mirror is moved is that the mirror movement Δx causes the optical path difference to change by an amount that is a multiple of the wavelength difference Δλ = |λ�� - λ₂|.
